models.sample_description: The analysis starts from the hand-classified 2002–2005 8-K restatement sample (83 errors and 105 irregularities; n=188). Errors were randomly sampled at about one quarter of the eligible error population while all irregularities were retained; the regression loses 16 observations to missing data, leaving 172 observations in each Table 5 fit. The models apply population-proportion weights to account for disproportionate sampling.
models.method_details: The authors state that they estimate logistic regressions. Table 5 reports weighted logistic estimates for the three turnover outcomes.

review_notes: Source-first selection: the paper proposes distinguishing errors from irregularities to test consequences of intentional versus unintentional misreporting for executive turnover. Table 5 is the principal multivariate test and reports separate full-control weighted logistic regressions for CEO, CFO, and CEO-or-CFO turnover. Retained all three outcome models and the primary 13-month window; excluded classification validation and descriptive comparisons, the alternative CAR-severity models in Table 6, and later PRE/POST analyses in Tables 8–9.

Needs review: Table 5 duplicates CFO Turnover in its first two printed headers while the results narrative discusses CEO first; Equation (1) and the Table 5 note conflict on the turnover-window anchor and CEO_EQUITY timing; SUBSIDIARY, IRREGULARITY, and ROA use differing wording across model definitions and the Table 5 note; CEO_EQUITY construction is not specified; Table 3 winsorization is not explicitly tied to the Table 5 regressions; fixed effects and the standard-error correction are unreported.
results_review_notes: Table 5 columns 1–3 are the only retained baseline result columns. Table 5 Pseudo-R², log likelihood, and n cells are retained as auxiliary fit-statistic rows; predicted probabilities discussed in prose and later sensitivity tests are not added.

Table 5 parenthetical values are chi-square statistics, not standard errors. The subtype, null, degrees of freedom, and reference distribution are not identified. Exact p-values are not reported; significance markers are preserved with the one-tailed-when-predicted note and row-specific alternatives only where the table prints a prediction sign.

The selected descriptive evidence is Table 3 for retained controls and Total Assets inputs used by ratios/size quintiles, plus Table 4 turnover percentages for retained outcomes. Table 3 precedes regression missing-data deletion; Table 4 error-frequency counts are weighted.

No separate descriptive rows are reported for IRREGULARITY, SUBSIDIARY, their interaction, ANNUAL, the retained CAR window, or the size-quintile indicators; no moments were calculated. Figures 1–2 report announcement-window CARs, not the retained CAR from days −240 to −8.
Table 3 and Table 4 group-comparison markers are preserved in reported labels; their t/Wilcoxon/chi-square tests are not represented as data-value statistics.
